      "evidence": "Traced path in tree 8c1f133b7. The test TestTickEndsCapabilityProbesAtTheFifthObservation confirms that probing stops after 4 probes. (3) remedyHealthRoles skips any role at AUTO_HEAL_ENDED (tick.go:640), so the steward never probes again. (4) capabilitySnapshotStatus keeps the runtime dead in two ways: the snapshot stays stale, and the failed probe record latches it (health.go:1805-1808: probe.Result == ComponentError && !newest.After(probe.LastCompletion)). (5) applyHealthObservation sets the failure count back to zero only when the role reads alive (health.go:831-846), so the breaker never re-arms. (6) The role has a lawful remedy, so it is never Standing (health.go:897-899), and fileStandingDefects never files a defect for it.       "title": "Once the five-observation breaker ends the steward's capability probing for a runtime, the capability-snapshots health role stays red indefinitely, and the public system check tells the person that 'the steward tick probes each runtime on PATH with a missing or stale snapshot and records a fresh snapshot'. That is false in this state: the steward has stopped probing. If the person fixes the cause the reason names (for example, runs 'claude auth login'), the role still does not recover. Only a later delegated job for that runtime, whose admission probe writes a fresh snapshot, or removing the runtime from metasystem.runtimes clears it. No standing defect is filed either, because the role counts as having a lawful remedy. The goal's intent requires a verdict that is 'red only for something someone can act on', where 'a role with no remedy after N ticks files one defect instead of staying red forever'. The slice works when probes succeed. It does not work for a runtime that is on PATH but whose login lapses, or was never set up, for five ticks; that state is reachable on an ordinary seat and recurs on every login lapse."
